- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). - claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.

<result># Background Workers/Runners Started by the Memos Server

This is a Go monorepo (the `usememos/memos` note-taking app), with a single server binary (`cmd/memos`) and a frontend SPA in `web/` (no runtime relevance). Everything below is about the Go server process.

## Entry point / bootstrap

- `/bench/repo/cmd/memos/main.go` — cobra `rootCmd.Run` (lines 36–107) is the bootstrap: creates the DB driver, calls `store.New(...)` (line 64), runs migrations, then `server.NewServer(...)` (line 76) and `s.Start(ctx)` (line 89).
- `/bench/repo/server/server.go` — `Server.Start` (line 101) starts the HTTP listener and, at line 129, calls `s.startBackgroundRunners(ctx)` (defined lines 153–174). This is the actual "what gets started" chokepoint for scheduled/recurring workers.

## Workers actually started

### 1. S3 presign runner — the only registered "background runner"
- Started at `/bench/repo/server/server.go:161-171`, inside `startBackgroundRunners`:
  - `s3presignRunner := s3presign.NewRunner(s.Store)` (line 162)
  - `s3presignRunner.RunOnce(ctx)` — runs immediately once at startup (line 163)
  - `go func() { s3presignRunner.Run(s3Context) }()` — launched as a goroutine, tracked via `backgroundRunnerWG`/`backgroundRunnerCancels` for graceful shutdown (lines 166-171)
- Scheduling mechanism: a plain `time.NewTicker` fixed interval loop, **not** cron. Defined in `/bench/repo/server/runner/s3presign/runner.go`:
  - `const runnerInterval = time.Hour * 12` (line 27, comment: "Schedule runner every 12 hours")
  - `Run(ctx)` (lines 29-41) does `ticker := time.NewTicker(runnerInterval)` and calls `r.RunOnce(ctx)` on every tick until `ctx.Done()`.
  - Purpose: re-presigns S3 object URLs for attachments whose presigned URL is within 4 days of its 5-day expiry (see `CheckAndPresign`, lines 47-131).

This is the **only** worker the server registers as a long-running/recurring background loop.

### 2. Store-level cache cleanup loops (started before the HTTP server, but still part of server startup)
- `/bench/repo/store/store.go:37-59` (`store.New`) creates three in-memory caches: `instanceSettingCache`, `userCache`, `userSettingCache` (lines 51-53), each via `cache.New(cacheConfig)` with `CleanupInterval: 5 * time.Minute` (line 42).
- `/bench/repo/store/cache/cache.go:75-84` (`cache.New`) spawns a goroutine per cache: `go c.cleanupLoop()` (line 82).
- Scheduling mechanism: `cleanupLoop` (lines 199-215) uses `time.NewTicker(c.config.CleanupInterval)` — a fixed 5-minute interval ticker, purely to evict expired TTL entries.
- `store.New(...)` is invoked from `/bench/repo/cmd/memos/main.go:64`, i.e. before `server.NewServer`/`s.Start`, so these three ticker-driven goroutines are indeed started as part of normal server bootstrap. Shutdown is via `Store.Close()` (`/bench/repo/store/store.go:72-79`), which calls `.Close()` on each cache to stop its goroutine, invoked from `Server.Shutdown` (`server.go:146`).

### 3. Fixed-size async worker pools (event-driven, not time-scheduled)
These are goroutine pools consuming from buffered channels, started via Go `init()` functions the moment the owning package is imported/linked into the binary (which happens because `server`/`cmd/memos` import them transitively) — not gated behind any explicit "start" call, and not schedule-driven at all, but they are recurring background consumers so worth listing:
- `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go:39-55` — `asyncPostQueue := make(chan *WebhookRequestPayload, 128)` (line 39); `init()` (lines 42-55) launches 4 goroutines that range over the channel and call `Post(payload)`. Trigger: whenever application code enqueues a webhook dispatch (event-driven consumer, not cron/interval).
- `/bench/repo/internal/email/email.go:14-36` — `asyncEmailQueue := make(chan asyncEmailRequest, 128)` (line 14); `init()` (lines 16-36) launches 2 goroutines that range over the channel and call `Send(...)`. Trigger: application code enqueuing an email send (event-driven).
- `/bench/repo/server/auth/authenticator.go:178-184` (`recordPATUsage`) — a one-off `go func(){...}()` per call to asynchronously update PAT last-used time; not a persistent worker/loop, just fire-and-forget per request.

### Not a background worker (event-driven, per-connection only)
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/sse_handler.go:64` — `heartbeat := time.NewTicker(sseHeartbeatInterval)` (30s, defined line 18) is created **per SSE client connection** inside `handleSSE`, not at server startup. It's request-scoped, not a global scheduled runner.

### Not a recurring worker (runs synchronously, once, on demand)
- `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go` — defines a `Runner` type with only `RunOnce(ctx)` (lines 27-72); there is no `Run`/loop/ticker in this package at all. Grepping usages shows it is **never instantiated via `NewRunner`/`RunOnce` as a background job** — instead only the standalone helper function `RebuildMemoPayload` (line 74) is called synchronously and inline from request handlers in `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:108` and `:447` (on memo create/update). So despite living under `server/runner/`, this "runner" is not started as a background process by the server; it's dead code as a runner and only its helper function is reused synchronously.

## Scheduling infrastructure present but NOT used by the server

**`/bench/repo/internal/scheduler/`** — a full, self-contained "GitHub Actions–inspired cron job scheduler" package with real cron-expression parsing (5- and 6-field), timezone support, middleware (Recovery/Logging/Timeout), and graceful shutdown:
- `scheduler.go` (`Scheduler`, `New`, `Register`, `Start`, `Stop` — types/funcs listed at lines 12, 54, etc.)
- `job.go` (`Job`, `JobHandler`)
- `parser.go` (cron expression parser, `Schedule` struct)
- `middleware.go` (`Recovery`, `Logging`, `Timeout` middleware)
- `doc.go` explicitly documents usage: `s := scheduler.New(); s.Register(&scheduler.Job{Schedule: "0 2 * * *", ...}); s.Start()`
- `README.md` markets it as production-ready with a comparison table vs. `robfig/cron` / `gocron`.

**It is never imported anywhere outside its own package.** I confirmed via `grep -rln "usememos/memos/internal/scheduler"` across the whole repo that the only files importing it are its own test files (`internal/scheduler/example_test.go`, `internal/scheduler/integration_test.go`) — i.e. it demonstrates and tests itself but is not wired into `cmd/memos/main.go`, `server/server.go`, or any router/service. No `scheduler.New(`/`.Register(`/`.Start(` call exists anywhere in `/bench/repo/server`, `/bench/repo/cmd`, or `/bench/repo/store`.

**Conclusion: `internal/scheduler` is fully-built, cron-capable scheduling infrastructure that the running server does NOT start or use at all** — it's effectively unused/leftover (or speculative/library-in-waiting) code, exercised only by its own test suite.

## Summary table

| Runner | Started at | Trigger/schedule | Wired into server? |
|---|---|---|---|
| S3 presign runner | `server/server.go:161-171` | `time.Ticker`, fixed 12h (`server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:27,30`) | Yes — only registered `backgroundRunner` |
| Cache cleanup ×3 (instance setting/user/user setting) | `store/store.go:51-53` via `cache.New` → `store/cache/cache.go:82` | `time.Ticker`, fixed 5min (`store/cache/cache.go:44`) | Yes — started during `store.New()` in `cmd/memos/main.go:64`, before `server.NewServer` |
| Webhook async dispatch pool (4 goroutines) | `internal/webhook/webhook.go:42-55` (package `init()`) | Event-driven, channel consumer (buffered chan, cap 128) | Yes — implicit at process load, no cron |
| Email async send pool (2 goroutines) | `internal/email/email.go:16-36` (package `init()`) | Event-driven, channel consumer (buffered chan, cap 128) | Yes — implicit at process load, no cron |
| SSE heartbeat ticker | `server/router/api/v1/sse_handler.go:64` | `time.Ticker`, 30s, but per-connection not global | Yes, but scoped to each SSE request, not a startup-time background runner |
| `memopayload.Runner` (Run/loop) | N/A | N/A | **Not started as a runner** — only its `RebuildMemoPayload` helper is called synchronously from `memo_service.go:108,447` |
| `internal/scheduler` (cron scheduler package) | N/A | Cron expressions (fully implemented) | **Never used** — only referenced by its own tests |</result>
